title: Price ranges with Monte Carlo, not one magic number

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody can say what Apple's stock will close at next year. But can you say how far it could reasonably swing?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds more honest than a single prediction. How do you do it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With a Monte Carlo simulation. Antoine took Apple's daily closes and split them at the first of January 2023. Everything before that is training data. Everything after is the hold-out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does he learn from the training part?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Daily log returns. From those he gets an average drift and a volatility, which is just how much the price tends to wiggle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thousands of times. Each simulated path draws a random shock every day, using the drift and the volatility, and pushes the price forward. There's a small correction term so the simulated average doesn't climb faster than real history justifies.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Think of it as releasing a crowd of tiny paper boats on a river and watching where they end up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. Then you read the fan of paths. The median and mean show the center. The fifth to ninety-fifth percentile gives a band for where the price might land. And the real hold-out prices show up as dots to compare.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For Apple, the mean simulated price after 364 days was about two hundred six dollars sixty-three, against a real close of one ninety-two fifty-three on the twenty-ninth of December 2023. That's a gap of about seven percent. He repeated it for Microsoft and for Apple again with 2024 closes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It answers a different question: which distribution fits the observed prices before simulating. The two combine well. This post covers the forward step.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Monte Carlo gives you the width of a range, and backtesting tests a trading rule. Keeping those questions separate keeps the thinking clear. The full write-up has the code and every fan chart.
